title: Reload a receipt printer with a new roll so the paper feeds out the front and the cover ends closed
instruction: The receipt printer has run out of paper. Fit the new roll so that the paper feeds out of the front slot, leave the cover closed, and let go with both fingers at least 3 cm from the printer and the roll.
context: Loading a new paper roll is an everyday chore at a till, a kitchen printer or a home label printer: the roll must unwind the way the printer expects or it prints blank, and it sits under a hinged cover that is held open while it goes in. Source: Epson TM-T20II User's Manual, Installing Roll Paper: "insert the roll paper. The correct direction of the paper is shown in the illustration below." (https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0026/6377/6307/files/tm-t20ii_Users_Manual.pdf). One hand holds the hinged cover open while the other turns the roll a quarter turn so its orange-taped free end leads toward the slot. Why a robot task: two hands, a spring hinge and an orientation read off the scene. Closest on the board: TK-S2ZZAS (lid held open). No receipt-roll card among 477 titles; new here: the free end decides the turn.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), z above the bench top (z = 0.7475 m, hardwood, friction 0.5). Materials: charcoal ABS printer, black ABS cover with a blue lift lip, white thermal paper on a brown cardboard core, black rubber stand. Printer (fixed, 25 kg stand-in for a bolted-down desktop printer, friction 1.2): 12 x 20 x 7 cm at (21.5, 0), x 15.5 to 27.5, z 0 to 7. Open-top paper bay with its floor at z 0.5: front posts x 15.5 to 17.5 (y +/-4.5 to +/-10) leave a 9 cm wide exit slot open to the cover, its floor flush with the chute; side walls y +/-6.5 to +/-10; rear wall x 25.0 to 27.5; bay 7.5 cm front to back (x 17.5 to 25.0). Two cradle shoulders (y +/-3.4 to +/-6.5, 1.5 cm tall) make a 6.8 cm wide roll channel and leave 13 cm between the walls for the gripper pads. Chute apron 6 x 10 x 0.5 cm in front (x 9.5 to 15.5). A status lamp (red, green or amber, display only) and a power button sit on the front face. Cover (hinged lid, 150 g): 11 x 20 x 0.8 cm plate hinged at its back top edge (x 27.5, z 7.0) with a return spring of 0.08 N m/rad, damping 0.2 N m s/rad. Grippable lift tab 2.4 x 2.4 x 2.0 cm at the front-left edge (y 11.8 to 14.2). The bay is open once the lid angle >= 50 degrees; a seated roll fits under the closed cover. Roll (loose, 90 g, friction 0.5): 58 mm wide, 60 mm across, 25 mm core; a rigid 12 x 5.8 x 0.3 cm paper strip (the free end, tipped with orange tape) runs from under it. Stand (fixed, 25 kg, friction 1.2): rubber plate 9 x 14 x 1 cm at (10, -14) with one chock 4 x 1.6 x 2.2 cm, 8.5 mm behind the roll on the +y side. At the start the roll's axis runs along x, its centre at (10, -14, z 4.3), and its free end runs toward -y. Correct seating: roll centre (21.0, 0, z 3.8), axis along y, free end toward -x on the floor and the chute, tip at x 9.0 (6.5 cm outside the front face). Both arms start open at ready (about (10, -/+14)). The layout is the same in every trial. Real build: a printed or sheet-metal printer bolted to the bench (this replaces the 25 kg mass), a real 58 mm thermal roll with a card strip taped to its end, and a 1 cm rubber pad on the bench.
scoring: Final state plus the run's facts. COVER CLOSED: the cover within 3 degrees of rest (0 degrees). SEATED: roll centre within 12 mm in x, 8 mm in y and 3 mm in z of (21.0, 0, z 3.8), axis within 5 degrees of y, level within 5 degrees. FEEDS: the paper's free end at x <= 13.5 cm (at least 2 cm outside the front face), within 2 cm of y 0 and below z 3.0 cm. RELEASED: both gripper centres at least 3 cm from the printer, cover and roll, and both grippers at least 90% open. STILL: the roll and the cover each move less than 1 mm over the last 1 s and the roll is slower than 1 cm/s. Zero: the printer or the stand is shifted more than 5 mm at any time (permanent); the roll ends seated with its free end toward the rear wall (+x); the roll ends anywhere other than on the stand or in the bay. 1.0: COVER CLOSED, SEATED, FEEDS, RELEASED, STILL. 0.75: the same but RELEASED or STILL fails. 0.5: SEATED and FEEDS with the cover not closed (held or stuck). Else 0 (lifting the roll and putting it back, or holding the cover open without loading, earns nothing). Doing nothing scores 0; a held or hovering roll does not count as seated. Possible scores: 0.0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial: tape (2 cm outside, 1.2 cm centring), an angle gauge for the closed cover, a top and a front photo.
fidelity: Real hinge lid on mechkit (stops 0 to 85 deg, spring 0.08 N m/rad) opened by lifting the front lip tab; a real printer's lid is latched. The printer is 7 cm tall (real about 14) so the lid stays within arm reach, and a fixed 25 kg stand-in. The front exit is a 9 cm notch for a rigid strip. The paper's free end is a rigid 3 mm strip (real paper bends); the roll does not spin and its core is solid. Lamp and tape are unscored markers.
reset_notes: Cover closed (lamp red); roll on its stand with its axis along x, its centre at (10, -14, z 4.3) and its free end running toward -y; both grippers open and clear at ready; bench clear. The first video frame shows the closed printer with a red lamp and the roll on its stand.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0. Scripted demo: 1.0 (cover held open by one hand, roll turned and seated by the other, cover let close). One arm left idle: 0.0.
